diagnosis.seal: combined-peerloss-diag-a1 (instrumented; os_log and file markers were both unavailable: the daemon writes nothing to the unified log, and file writes appear to go through the browser broker, so they fail once the browser is gone)
diagnosis.samples: After a browser abort the ReadyPulse and AuthorityLoop threads had returned (peer loss detected, supplied SIGTERM shutdown requested; port 21520 closed). Main stayed in uv_run; the only other live source was libuv's FSEvents run loop: chokidar watchers opened via auxBrokerBoundary().watcher (memory manager, loop runtimes) that the supplied shutdown never closes. A later SIGTERM re-runs the idempotent shutdown, so it looks ignored.
diagnosis.second stage: With node::Stop after 10 s the loop returned, then main waited forever in the worker drain: browser grant retirement stays pending until a browser peer proves teardown.

change: After observed peer loss: node::Stop if the loop has not returned 10 s after the supplied shutdown was requested; then, if the worker drain is still unresolved 10 s later, Refuse("parent-loss-drain") and _exit(75) with no disposal or clean claim. JS lifeline edit dropped: index.mjs and aux-native-entry.mjs are back to their pre-Batch-1 bytes.

build.reproducibility: unmodified main.o rebuilds with identical code, symbols and section sizes; only DWARF accelerator tables and debug strings differ

observed.abort: observed: daemon exited 21 s after SIGABRT to the browser
observed.relaunchAfterAbort: observed: relaunch started normally; daemon listening after 25 s (previously refused with "paired daemon receipt")
observed.quit: observed twice: Quit completes, but slowly: browser exited 17 s and daemon 37 s after Quit (the daemon leaves through the new peer-loss bound). On the Batch 1 seal, whose JS edit exited 10 s after a requested shutdown, both had exited within 8 s.

open: Normal Quit is slow because the supplied shutdown never closes the chokidar watchers, so the loop does not end while the browser waits.
